paper.title: Bandit Online Optimization Over the Permutahedron

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit linear optimization over the (symmetrized) permutahedron with losses bounded by 1 (s_t in the dual polytope)
unmapped: actions are the n! vertices (permutations) of the n-permutahedron in R^n, d = n
settings.definition_quote: For this section, we will assume that the instantaneous losses are uniformly bounded by $1$, in absolute value: For all $t$ and $\cent{\pi}\in\cent{S}_n$, $|\cent{\pi}'s_t|\leq 1$. Equivalently, using geometric language, the loss vectors belong to a polytope which is \emph{dual} to the permutahedron.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit linear optimization over the rescaled symmetrized permutahedron Q_n with ||s_t||_1 <= 1
unmapped: actions are vertices of the permutahedron rescaled into [-1,1]^n (Q_n = 2/(n-1) P_n), d = n
settings.definition_quote: We will be working under the more restricted assumption that $\sup \|s_t\|_1 \leq 1$ and $\sup \|{\cent{\pi}}_t\|_\infty \leq 1$. This in particular implies that $|\cent{\pi}_t' s_t|\leq 1$, as before.

conditions: |pi' s_t| <= 1 for all permutations pi and all t

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: If algorithm $\banditrank$ (Algorithm~\ref{alg:main}) is executed with parameters $\gamma = O({{n^{3/2}}/\sqrt{T}})$ and $\eta = O(\gamma/n)$, then the expected regret (with respect to the game defined by the symmetrized permutahedron) is at most $ O(n^{3/2}\sqrt T)$. The running time of each iteration is $O(n^3)$. Additionally, there exists an algorithm with the same expected regret bound and running time with respect to the standard permutahedron...

results.notes: Paper's n (ground set size) mapped to d. Running time O(n^3) per step. Same bound claimed for the standard permutahedron variant (assuming |pi's_t|<=1). Adversary type not stated explicitly; regret is E[L_T] - L*_T.

conditions: ||s_t||_1 <= 1 and actions are vertices of Q_n subset [-1,1]^n

source.label: thm:osmd
source.quote: For $\eta=O(n\sqrt{1/T})$ and $\gamma=O(\sqrt{1/T})$, Algorithm $\OSMDrank$ has expected regret $O(n\sqrt{T})$ and running time $O(n^2 +n\tau(n))$ per step, where $\tau(n)$ is the time for a numerical optimization step depending on $n$. Additionally, there exists an algorithm with the same expected regret bound and running time with respect to the standard permutahedron (assuming $\|s_t\|_1 \leq 1/n$).

results.notes: Proof is a sketch. Running time O(n^2 + n tau(n)), tau(n)=O(n^2) in fixed precision. Same bound for standard permutahedron under ||s_t||_1 <= 1/n.
